generate_badge.description: Create a static badge with a label, message, and color: the classic 'subject | status' badge. Add a logo or a custom style to match your project's look.
generate_badge.name: generate_badge

parameters.description: Left-side text (the subject), for example 'build' or 'coverage'.
parameters.name: label

parameters.description: Right-side text (the status), for example 'passing' or '98%'.
parameters.name: message

parameters.description: Badge color: a named color (brightgreen, green, yellow, orange, red, blue, lightgrey, etc.) or a hex code such as 4c1 or 2ea44f.
parameters.name: color

parameters.description: Badge visual style. Defaults to flat when omitted.
parameters.name: style

parameters.description: Optional named logo to show before the label (a Simple Icons slug, e.g. github, python, docker).
parameters.name: logo

parameters.description: Optional color for the logo (a named color or hex code).
parameters.name: logo_color

parameters.description: Set to 'auto' to shrink a wide logo to fit the badge height. Only applies to Simple Icons logos.
parameters.name: logo_size

parameters.description: Optional background color for the label (left) side of the badge.
parameters.name: label_color

parameters.description: HTTP cache lifetime for the badge, in seconds. Shields.io ignores a value below its own per-badge default (300 for most badges), so this can only make a badge refresh less often, never more.
parameters.name: cache_seconds

is_error.description: True when Shields.io could not build the badge and rendered one of its own error messages instead ('inaccessible', 'no result', 'not found', ...).

label.description: The left-side text as Shields.io rendered it (empty for a message-only badge or the social style).

markdown.description: Markdown image snippet ready to paste into a README.

message.description: The right-side text as Shields.io rendered it. For a dynamic, regex, endpoint, or service badge this is the live value that was extracted.

svg.description: The raw SVG markup of the rendered badge.

generate_dynamic_badge.description: Create a badge whose message is pulled live from a remote JSON, XML, YAML, or TOML document. Shields.io fetches the URL and applies your query to extract the value to display. The extracted value is returned as 'message' so later steps can use it too.

generate_dynamic_badge.name: generate_dynamic_badge

parameters.name: data_url

parameters.description: Selector for the value: a JSONPath for JSON, YAML, and TOML (e.g. $.version) or an XPath for XML.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Format of the source document. Defaults to JSON.
parameters.name: data_type

parameters.description: Left-side text (the subject) for the badge.
parameters.name: label

parameters.description: Optional badge color: a named color or a hex code. Defaults to Shields.io's own coloring when omitted.

generate_regex_badge.description: Create a badge whose message is found by a regular expression in any remote text file: a README, a changelog, a config file. Shields.io fetches the URL, takes the first match, and shows it (or your rewritten version of it) as the badge message.
generate_regex_badge.display_str_template: Generate a Shields.io regex badge from {0}.
generate_regex_badge.name: generate_regex_badge

parameters.description: URL of the text file to search.
parameters.name: data_url

parameters.description: An RE2 regular expression. Only the first match is used. Capture groups, named (?<name>...) or numbered, can be referenced from 'replace'.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: Optional rewrite of the match: $1 inserts the first capture group, $<name> a named group, $$ a literal dollar sign. Leave empty to show the whole match.
parameters.name: replace

parameters.description: Optional regex flags, any combination of i (case-insensitive), m (multi-line), and s (dot matches newlines), for example 'im'.
parameters.name: flags

description: Generate dynamic SVG badges for your README, docs, or dashboards with Shields.io's keyless badge API. Build static 'subject | status' badges, version and license badges, dynamic badges that pull a live value from a JSON, XML, YAML, or TOML document or a regex match in any text file, endpoint badges driven by your own JSON, and any of the hundreds of ready-made service badges (GitHub stars, npm downloads, PyPI version, CI status). No account or API key required.
